```{r load, include=FALSE}
suppressPackageStartupMessages({ library(tidyverse); library(janitor); library(knitr) })
invisible(lapply(list.files("R", pattern = "\\.R$", full.names = TRUE), source))

raw_path <- "data/raw/sleep_wellbeing_raw.csv"
if (!file.exists(raw_path)) {
  source("R/generate_data.R")
  dir.create("data/raw", recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
  readr::write_csv(generate_sleep_wellbeing(), raw_path)
}
raw <- readr::read_csv(raw_path, col_types = cols(.default = col_character()))
report  <- build_validation_report(raw)
cleaned <- clean_dataset(raw)
num_cols <- c("age","sleep_hours","caffeine_cups","screen_time_hours",
              "exercise_days_per_week","stress_level","wellbeing_score")
```

> **All data in this report is SYNTHETIC and fictional.** It was generated by
> `R/generate_data.R` for the sole purpose of demonstrating a reproducible
> data-quality and analysis workflow. It does not describe real people and
> must not be interpreted as empirical evidence about sleep or wellbeing.

# Introduction

This report demonstrates a fully reproducible data-analysis workflow in R. We
take a deliberately messy synthetic dataset of hypothetical sleep patterns and
self-reported wellbeing, validate its quality, clean it with transparent and
documented functions, and then produce descriptive statistics, frequency
tables, correlations and publication-style figures.

# Methodology

The workflow is organised as independent, testable R functions:

* **Generation** (`R/generate_data.R`) — creates a reproducible synthetic
  dataset (`set.seed(42)`) in which wellbeing genuinely depends on sleep,
  stress, exercise and caffeine, and then *injects* realistic data-quality
  problems (missing values, duplicates, inconsistent labels, impossible values).
* **Validation** (`R/validate.R`) — inspects the raw data without modifying it:
  missing values, exact duplicates, out-of-range entries and inconsistent
  category labels.
* **Cleaning** (`R/clean.R`) — operates on a *copy* of the raw data (the
  original is always preserved), standardises missingness, coerces numeric
  columns, nulls impossible values, canonicalises categories and removes
  duplicate rows.
* **Analysis** (`R/analysis.R`) — descriptive statistics, `janitor::tabyl`
  frequency tables and Pearson correlations with hypothesis tests.
* **Figures** (`R/figures.R`) — `ggplot2` publication-style graphics.
* **Tests** (`tests/testthat/`) — automated `testthat` tests on tiny datasets
  with known expected results.

## Raw data quality

```{r validation}
knitr::kable(report$missing, caption = "Missing values per column (raw data)")
knitr::kable(report$out_of_range, caption = "Out-of-range / invalid numeric entries (raw data)")
knitr::kable(head(report$gender_labels, 10), caption = "Raw gender labels (inconsistent)")
cat("Exact duplicate rows detected:", report$n_duplicate_rows, "\n")
```

## Effect of cleaning

```{r cleaning-effect}
tibble(
  stage = c("raw", "cleaned"),
  rows  = c(nrow(raw), nrow(cleaned))
) %>% knitr::kable(caption = "Row counts before and after cleaning")
```

# Results

## Descriptive statistics

```{r desc}
knitr::kable(descriptive_stats(cleaned, num_cols),
             caption = "Descriptive statistics (cleaned data)")
```

## Frequency tables

```{r freq}
knitr::kable(frequency_table(cleaned, gender), caption = "Gender")
knitr::kable(frequency_table(cleaned, sleep_quality), caption = "Sleep quality")
```

## Correlations

```{r corr}
knitr::kable(round(correlation_matrix(cleaned, num_cols), 2),
             caption = "Pearson correlation matrix (cleaned data)")

key <- bind_rows(
  cor_test_pair(cleaned, "sleep_hours", "wellbeing_score"),
  cor_test_pair(cleaned, "stress_level", "wellbeing_score"),
  cor_test_pair(cleaned, "exercise_days_per_week", "wellbeing_score")
)
knitr::kable(key, caption = "Key correlations with wellbeing (with p-values)")
```

## Figures

```{r figs}
fig_sleep_hist(cleaned)
fig_sleep_wellbeing(cleaned)
fig_wellbeing_by_quality(cleaned)
fig_corr_heatmap(cleaned, num_cols)
```

# Limitations

* **The data is entirely synthetic.** Relationships shown here were built into
  the data-generating process by construction; they are **not** evidence about
  real human sleep or wellbeing.
* Cleaning decisions (valid ranges, label mappings) are explicit assumptions
  defined in `R/clean.R`; different assumptions would yield different results.
* Invalid and missing values are set to `NA` rather than imputed, so analyses
  use pairwise-complete observations and sample sizes vary across correlations.
* Correlation does not imply causation; no causal claims are made.
* No real participants, institutions, supervisors or publications are involved.
